profiles.title: The Pochaev Icon of the Mother of God
profiles.subject: Theotokos

overview.text: The Pochaev icon is associated with the Dormition monastery in southwest Ukraine. Father Alexander Golubov’s historical account distinguishes written evidence about the monastery and the icon’s donation from local traditions concerning earlier apparitions.

sourceRefs.locator: Opening description; early history and endowment

overview.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published source; substantial verbatim reproduction is not licensed. This is an editorial summary, not the source author’s wording.

blocks.text: Golubov describes Mary holding Christ on her right arm and a cloth covering his feet. The child blesses; seven smaller saints appear along the sides and bottom. The displayed image shows the decorated shrine around this particular Mother-and-Child composition.

sourceRefs.locator: Opening paragraph: description of the icon

blocks.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published source; substantial verbatim reproduction is not licensed. This is an editorial summary, not the source author’s wording.

blocks.text: His account connects the icon with Metropolitan Neophyte’s visit in 1559 and his gift to Anna Goiskaya. Anna’s 1597 endowment transferred the icon to the monastery. A distinct local tradition places an apparition and footprint at Mount Pochaev around 1340.

sourceRefs.locator: Metropolitan Neophyte; Anna Goiskaya; footprint tradition

blocks.text: The OCA’s July 23 commemoration concerns deliverance from the siege of 1675. Its narrative describes the Mother of God and Saint Job appearing above the monastery. It also identifies monastery books as records of reported healings and other miracles.
